issues.subject: practical payroll steps for salary and overtime payment

claims.text: Under the Employment Act, ordinary salary and overtime payments do not have the same payment deadline after the end of the salary period. Ordinary salary must be paid within 7 days after the end of the salary period, whereas payment for overtime work must be made within 14 days after the last day or end of the salary period.

refs.completeAdmittedPassage: For overtime work, your employer must pay you at least 1.5 times the hourly basic rate of pay. Payment must be made within 14 days after the last day of the salary period.

refs.completeAdmittedPassage: In accordance with the Employment Act, your employer must pay your salary at least once a month and within 7 days after the end of the salary period. There are exceptions for overtime, resignation without notice and other situations.

claims.text: Practical payroll execution requires employers covered by the Employment Act to issue itemised pay slips and keep detailed employment records, including salary records. Furthermore, salary must be paid on a working day during working hours and at the employee's place of work or another agreed location, with payment made directly into the employee's bank account or by cheque that needs to be cleared by the bank before the employee is considered paid.
